items.title: Live: Iran denies Trump's claims of 'very good' talks as initial strike deadline passes
items.description: US President Donald Trump says there have been "major points of agreement" in US-Iran talks to end the war, but Iran denies those claims. Follow live.

items.title: Iran launches longest-ever ballistic missile reaching beyond Middle East
items.description: An attempted attack on a US-UK military base in the Indian Ocean by Iran shows Tehran can launch missiles as far as 4,000km, raising concerns European cities are in reach.

items.title: With Trump's backtrack, a new reality emerges in the Iran war
items.description: In the wake of Donald Trump's backtrack, Iran realises more clearly than ever that it wields a potent new weapon on the global stage.

items.title: Global financial markets on war footing as 'situation remains incredibly fragile'
items.description: A key factor for shares, bonds, commodities and currencies remains consistently unchanged — the Strait of Hormuz is still effectively closed.

items.title: Live: Australia Post more than doubles fuel surcharges, as oil shocks continue
items.description: In other finance and business news today, Australian shares are higher, while the Australian dollar has dropped under 70 cents to the greenback. Follow live.

items.title: Shock election result likely as anti-Trump sentiment reaches Denmark
items.description: When Donald Trump threatened to annex Greenland, Denmark leader Mette Frederiksen was flailing in the polls. Having stood up to the US president, she looks to have salvaged her political career.

items.title: Farmers rubbish 'worst ever' EU free trade agreement
items.description: The National Farmers' Federation says the deal will leave farmers without meaningful access to the EU market.

items.title: EU leader talks of 'upside down' world in grim address to parliament
items.description: The Europe Commission president declares that Europe and Australia must rearm and decarbonise as they try to break economic and energy dependencies on China and Russia.

items.title: Iran fuel shock turns EV uptake into a matter of national security
items.description: From UN leaders to former Australian Defence Force chiefs, a growing chorus of voices argues that dependence on fossil fuels is not just a climate issue, but a national security risk — exposing countries to volatile prices and supply shocks.

items.title: BOM website creator's new $16m contract has climate scientists worried
items.description: The company responsible for the highly criticised BOM website wins a $16 million tender to build a new climate data website for the government.

items.title: Growing links between organised crime and foreign 'despots', AFP boss warns
items.description: The Australian Federal Police is warning that foreign intelligence agencies are increasingly working with locally-based organised criminals to carry out "serious crimes", including terrorism, within Australia.

items.title: Tropical Cyclone Narelle to re-form and possibly intensify to category four
items.description: Coastal communities in the Kimberley region will be affected in the next 24 hours as Tropical Cyclone Narelle, which had been downgraded to a low, intensifies back to cyclone level.

items.title: Live: Coalition ramps up pressure on government over fuel shortages
items.description: The Coalition is keeping the pressure on the federal government over fuel supply gaps in regional Australia. Follow live.

items.title: 'Blue blob' vandal who gave sculpture googly eyes ordered to pay compensation
items.description: A 20-year-old woman who made headlines by putting googly eyes on a controversial sculpture in the middle of Mount Gambier is ordered to pay $2,000 to the city's council.

items.title: How Bron Lewis speed ran the Australian comedy scene
items.description: The crimson-haired comedian has gone from tiny open mics to the biggest stage in Melbourne in just a few short years.

items.title: I was in so much pain, I couldn't interact the same ways as other mums
items.description: Megan Blin says her chronic pain made it difficult to do things other first-time mums could.

items.title: The Diary of Anne Frank's 'uplifting' theatre production arrives at the right time
items.description: While considering it a "big responsibility" bringing the theatre production to Sydney at this time, actress Chloe-Jean Vincent says Anne Frank's story makes theatregoers feel "inspired and so uplifted".

items.title: When the 'orange people' moved in, this tiny WA town fought back
items.description: When the Rajneesh sect moved into a small town in Western Australia, the group didn't count on the strength of the local community fighting back.

items.title: Teachers in Victoria go on strike for the first time in 13 years
items.description: Some 35,000 people gathered for a rally in Melbourne CBD as teachers, principals and education support staff statewide stopped work for 24 hours.

items.title: Pastoral company fined record $45,000 for Queensland biosecurity breaches
items.description: A pastoral company has been hit with a record $45,000 fine after moving thousands of cattle across state lines without proper tracking. Authorities say the penalty sends a clear warning.

items.title: Community fears proposed law reform could erode Indigenous land rights
items.description: Aboriginal councils who have fought for decades to secure ancestral land are concerned proposed law reform puts rights at risk.

items.title: Termination of Jackie O's contract after complaint 'peculiar', lawyer says
items.description: A Sydney-based employment lawyer says the network who owns radio station KIIS FM acted "prematurely" when it cancelled the controversial Kyle and Jackie O Show.

items.title: Controller appears to say 'I messed up' after deadly runway crash
items.description: Audio recordings from New York's LaGuardia airport reveal an air traffic controller appearing to admit he "messed up" just moments after an Air Canada Express regional jet crashed into a fire truck, killing the pilot and co-pilot.

items.title: How '30 years of ambiguity' led to Iran's proxies hiding throughout Lebanon
items.description: Lebanon's justice minister accuses the Iranian-backed militant group Hezbollah of effectively giving Israel an excuse to attack the country amid threats of an Israeli occupation of the south.

items.title: E-bike ban to target Queenslanders who are 'medically unfit to drive'
items.description: Queenslanders who are not "medically fit to drive" will be banned from e-bikes and e-scooters.
